answers.answer: Build three tiers separately: top card is 1 randomly dealt Conflict I; next are 5 randomly dealt Conflict II; bottom are all 4 Conflict III in shuffled order. Shuffle every tier before selecting; return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking.
answers.evidence: Setup: ‘1 card randomly dealt’ from I, ‘5’ from II, ‘all 4’ III; return unused without looking.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; 3 troops in their garrison and 9 in supply (12 troops total); 1 water; one cube at the bottom of each of four Influence tracks; and 0 VP in a 3-player game or 1 VP in a 4-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 5–8 specify Agents, 12 troops (3 in garrison), bottom Influence spaces, water, and Score marker 1 in 4-player, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. You may Reveal with Agents remaining. After your Reveal turn your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turns, not after your Reveal turn has ended.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: ‘you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left’; after Reveal, turns skipped; Plot cards during own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one hand card face up with an Agent icon matching the destination’s icon; one card sends only one Agent, and a card with no Agent icons cannot be used. Send one Agent to an unoccupied space, meet requirements and pay entry costs immediately before resolving effects. If unable to pay, you cannot send the Agent there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: play one card to send one Agent; matching icon; unoccupied; costs paid immediately before effects.

answers.answer: No. Entry costs must be paid before resolving any board or card effects, so the card’s spice gain cannot cover a Conspire cost when you have only 3 spice. Once entry is paid, resolve the space effect, Agent box and one-space Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent-turn costs ‘paid immediately, before resolving any effects’; effects gained ‘in any order, after paying the entry cost.’

answers.answer: You may deploy the 3 troops recruited this turn (2 from the space plus 1 from the card) and up to 2 more from your garrison, for a maximum of 5. Recruited troops not deployed stay in your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its recruits go to the garrison and cannot normally be deployed then.
answers.evidence: Combat-space deployment: any/all troops recruited this turn plus up to two more from garrison; Rally Troops is not a Combat space.

answers.answer: Reveal in order: reveal remaining hand cards; resolve their Reveal boxes in any order (not boxes from cards played on Agent turns); set Combat strength; clean up. At Clean Up, put all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn’s four numbered steps; boxes are on ‘cards you just revealed’; Clean Up discards all cards in front of you.

answers.answer: Yes, refill the Imperium Row immediately after an acquisition and you may buy its replacement if affordable. You may pool Persuasion from sources for one card and split one source across cards. Persuasion cannot be saved; acquired cards go to your discard pile and are not used immediately. An Acquire box resolves once when the card is acquired.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: refill Row immediately; pool/split Persuasion; unused Persuasion lost; acquired cards go to discard and aren’t used right away; Acquire box at acquisition.

answers.answer: 3 troops are 6 strength and 4 revealed swords add 4, for 10 total. If your last Conflict troop is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased, including by swords. Above 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each Conflict troop = 2, each revealed sword = 1; without a troop strength is 0; over 20 flip marker to +20 and start again.

answers.answer: Starting with the First Player and proceeding clockwise, each player with at least one Conflict troop may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. A pass does not bind later turns; resolve combat after all involved players pass consecutively. Play ‘when you win’ cards after winning, before the next phase; if drawn as a victory reward, such a card may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue cards paragraph: order, eligible players, consecutive passes, win-trigger timing and reward-draw exception.

answers.answer: A and B tie for first, so neither wins and each gets the second reward. C and D compete for third; C takes the third reward and D gets none. A tie for second gives each tied player the third reward, even in 2- or 3-player games; a tie for third gives nothing. A player at 0 strength gets no reward. After rewards, troops return to supply.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: first-place tie gets second reward each; other players still compete for third; second-place tie gets third each; third tie nothing; 0 strength no reward; troops to supply.

answers.answer: In Phase 4: Makers, check The Great Flat, Hagga Basin and Imperial Basin. Put 1 spice from the bank on each space with no Agent, accumulating with prior bonus spice. Normal harvesting happens when a player sends an Agent to a Maker space, gaining that space’s base spice plus its bonus. If an Agent moves away and the space is empty in Phase 4, it gets bonus spice then.
answers.evidence: Makers phase lists three spaces and empty-space bonus; board-space table lists Maker harvest amounts; Maker spaces clarification says spice accumulates if empty in Phase 4.

answers.answer: The game ends at the end of the round in Recall if any player has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty; reaching 10 mid-round does not end it immediately. Resolve Endgame Intrigue cards before declaring the most-VP winner. Tiebreak order: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: end trigger at end of round; Endgame Intrigue first; full listed tiebreakers. Recall says check 10 VP or empty deck.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence you gain 1 VP and lose it if you drop below 2; you regain it on reaching 2 again. The 4-Influence bonus is retained if you later drop below 4 and can be earned again by dropping back and advancing. The first player at 4 takes the Alliance and its VP; an opponent takes it by rising higher, not by merely tying. If the holder was tied and loses Influence, a previously tied player takes the token.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence and Alliances sections specify 2-VP reversal, retained/re-earnable 4 bonus, first Alliance and passing/tied-holder rules.

answers.answer: If you lose 1 from 5 while tied with two opponents, one of those tied opponents takes the Alliance; when several were tied, you choose one. If instead you were the only player at 4 and fall to 3, you lose the token; with no player at 4+ to take it, return it to the board.
answers.evidence: Alliances: if holder loses Influence while previously tied, previously tied player takes it; if several tied, holder chooses. Falling to 3 or less returns it if nobody at 4+.

answers.answer: Discarding normally means a card from your hand and puts it in your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from hand, discard pile or play to the box; a Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or instructed to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle early just to inspect an empty deck’s top card.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards paragraph; standalone black-X optional, cost/self-trash exceptions; deck exhaustion clarification says cannot reshuffle early to look at top card.

answers.answer: The controller gains 1 Solari whenever any player, including the controller, visits Arrakeen or Carthag, or 1 spice for Imperial Basin. Winning a Conflict that rewards control places your Control marker on that space’s flag, replacing an opponent’s. When a matching Conflict is revealed later, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control rule gives visit bonuses, marker replacement, and optional defensive deployment from supply on matching Conflict reveal.

answers.answer: Use an unused color; put a cube at the bottom of each Influence track, remaining cubes in supply, no troops in garrison; remove the three 1P Arrakeen cards, shuffle remaining House Hagal cards, and give it three Agents. After each First Player Agent turn, it takes one turn if it has an Agent, up to three; it never Reveals. It does not collect resources, build a deck, earn Conflict rewards or VP, or claim Control, but it can hold Alliances.
answers.evidence: House Hagal setup, Agent turns and overview paragraphs state each item.

answers.answer: If the indicated space is occupied, reveal another card until an eligible unoccupied space appears; on a two-space card, use only the condition-matching option and if occupied draw again, never switch. Reshuffle immediately when the deck empties or Reshuffle appears. Ignore space costs, requirements and effects; resolve only card icons/instructions. Troop icons recruit, deploying to Conflict at Combat spaces; additionally it automatically deploys up to two garrison troops on any Combat-space turn. Harvest Spice chooses the Maker space with most bonus spice, tie-breaks on total base plus bonus, and if none has bonus spice reveals another card; removed bonus spice goes back to bank.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns, troops and Harvest Spice procedure specify all listed behavior.

answers.answer: If it has troops in the Conflict, at the start of Combat reveal a House Hagal card, reshuffling and revealing again if it is Reshuffle; add only its sword icons to 2 per deployed troop. Humans then play Combat Intrigue. Hagal receives no reward but occupies its rank. Human second-place ties each receive the third reward, even though ordinary third place pays nothing. If Hagal wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker; Hagal does not replace it.
answers.evidence: Combat strength procedure and aftermath explicitly state sequencing, ranks, tie, and Control.

answers.answer: At Round Start reveal a Conflict card and each player draws 5 cards. At ordinary Recall, return the Mentat to its designated space if needed, recall Agents to Leaders, pass the First Player marker clockwise, then begin the next round. A Sort Through the Chaos winner takes the Mentat at the start of the next round.
answers.evidence: Round Start, Recall and official FAQ timing paragraphs.

answers.answer: The bank’s Solari, spice and water are not limited; substitute if they run out. Troops are limited by your supply: if it is out of troops, you cannot recruit more until some return.
answers.evidence: Setup: resource tokens ‘are not limited; substitute if you run out’; Recruiting: cannot recruit while supply is out.

answers.answer: Each Leader has a unique ability used as described on the Leader and a Signet Ring ability activated when you play your Signet Ring card on an Agent turn. Cards of any type can override usual game rules.
answers.evidence: Overview: two unique abilities and Signet Ring timing; cards can override usual rules.

answers.answer: Sietch Tabr is a City-icon space requiring 2+ Fremen Influence; it recruits a troop and gains 1 water, and is a Combat space. You cannot enter at 1 Influence and use the card effect to reach 2, because entry requirements must be met before effects resolve.
answers.evidence: Board table lists City icon, requirement and effects; Combat list includes Sietch Tabr; costs/requirements are checked before effects.

answers.answer: Combat spaces are Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr, Research Station, Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Heighliner, Hardy Warriors and Stillsuits. Research Station and The Great Flat are Combat spaces; Conspire is not.
answers.evidence: Complete list of Combat spaces names these ten; says Conspire is not among them.

answers.answer: Wealth (Emperor): no cost; +1 Emperor Influence and 2 Solari. Conspire (Emperor): 4 spice; +1 Emperor Influence, 5 Solari, 2 troops and an Intrigue card. Foldspace (Spacing Guild): no cost; +1 Guild Influence and acquire Foldspace. Heighliner (Spacing Guild): 6 spice; +1 Guild Influence, 5 troops and 2 water. Secrets (Bene Gesserit): no cost; +1 Influence, draw Intrigue; each opponent with 4+ Intrigue gives one at random. Selective Breeding (Bene Gesserit): 2 spice; +1 Influence, trash a card and draw two. Stillsuits (Fremen): no cost; +1 Influence and 1 water. Hardy Warriors (Fremen): 1 water; +1 Influence and 2 troops.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table gives icon, entry cost and effects for all eight.

answers.answer: Arrakeen (City), no cost: recruit 1 troop, draw a card; controller gets 1 Solari. Carthag (City), no cost: recruit 1, draw Intrigue; controller gets 1 Solari. Research Station (City), 2 water: draw 3. Secure Contract (Spice Trade), no cost: 3 Solari. Imperial Basin (Spice Trade), no cost: 1 spice plus bonus; controller gets 1 spice. Hagga Basin (Spice Trade), 1 water: 2 spice plus bonus. Great Flat (Spice Trade), 2 water: 3 spice plus bonus.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table lists each cost, effect and controller benefit; Maker space classifications identify the icons.

answers.answer: Sell Melange has the Spice Trade icon. Exchange 2/3/4/5 spice for 6/8/10/12 Solari respectively; one exchange per turn.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table: Sell Melange; Spice Trade list includes it; table says one exchange per turn.

answers.answer: High Council costs 5 Solari, once per game; place your Councilor token on an unoccupied Council seat and gain 2 Persuasion during each Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Swordmaster costs 8 Solari, once per game; gain your third Agent and place it on your Leader, available for the rest of the game including that round.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table gives costs, once-per-game limits and benefits/timing.

answers.answer: Hall of Oratory has no cost, recruits 1 troop, and gives 1 Persuasion during your Reveal if your Agent is there. Rally Troops costs 4 Solari and recruits 4 troops to your garrison (not a Combat space). Mentat costs 2 Solari and draws a card; if Mentat is there, take it as an Agent for this round and return it at Recall.
answers.evidence: Board spaces table lists costs, recruits/card draw/Persuasion and Mentat use/return.

answers.answer: Yes. The recalled Agent returns to your Leader and may be used on another Agent turn in the same round. It does not reopen Agent turns once you have Revealed.
answers.evidence: Recall effects clarification states both points.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed on your Reveal turn remain face up in play until Clean Up unless trashed first. Fremen Bond works if at least one other Fremen card is in play; two Fremen Bond cards enable one another regardless of play order.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond clarification.

answers.answer: A single gain-two-Influence effect cannot be split between Factions. Alliance-icon effects require holding that Faction’s Alliance; numeric Influence-requirement icons require at least the shown Influence with that Faction.
answers.evidence: Conditional icons clarification states all three rules.

answers.answer: Keep Intrigue cards face down and separate from your deck; you may look at your own at any time and reveal them only when played. Discard played cards face up next to the Intrigue Deck; if it empties, shuffle discards into a new deck. Plot is played on your own Agent or Reveal turn, Combat only during Combat, Endgame only at game end. Intrigue card costs and conditions must be met. The summary does not specify whether other players may inspect your unplayed Intrigue cards.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards section covers privacy, destination, timing and reshuffle; Agent turn rule says Intrigue costs/conditions must be met. Opponents’ inspection rights are unstated.

answers.answer: Yes. A delayed Plot such as Charisma or Recruitment Mission may be played during your Agent turn; leave it face up until your next Reveal turn, use it then, and discard it.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards: delayed Plot may be played on Agent turn, left until Reveal, used then and discarded.

answers.answer: A card drawn during your Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used that turn, so it cannot become an Agent turn. A card drawn after your Reveal turn stays in your hand for next round, when you still draw five more cards.
answers.evidence: Reveal effects step specifies both timings.

answers.answer: Most effects are mandatory unless they say ‘may,’ use an optional arrow, or optional black-X trash. An ordinary card’s optional arrow payment/effect may be declined; board entry costs must be paid, and Intrigue costs/conditions must be met. Standalone black-X trash is optional; trashing to pay a cost is required; a non-arrow instruction to trash itself is mandatory. A paid optional arrow effect resolves once and cannot be repeated by paying again.
answers.evidence: Agent turn effect/cost paragraph spells out optionality, entry and Intrigue requirements, self-trash and no-repeat rule.

answers.answer: Play Bindu Suspension at the start of your Agent turn, before anything else. Draw a card, then immediately end your turn; you cannot continue that turn’s actions.
answers.evidence: Rulebook clarification: Bindu Suspension timing, draw, and immediate end of turn.

answers.answer: Calculated Hire can take the Mentat only from its starting Landsraad space, not from another player or another space. For Sort Through the Chaos, take it at the start of the next round and use it that round.
answers.evidence: Calculated Hire and Mentat reward clarifications.

answers.answer: Yes, Kwisatz Haderach permits an Agent turn with no unused Agents by sending an Agent already on a board space, including back to the same space. It cannot reuse High Council or Swordmaster, and cannot overcome The Voice.
answers.evidence: Kwisatz Haderach clarification states each restriction and permission.

answers.answer: The Voice stops opponents, including via Kwisatz Haderach, from sending Agents to the chosen space for one turn; remove its marker on your next turn. Mark the space with one of your available Control markers.
answers.evidence: The Voice clarification gives marker, removal timing and effect.

answers.answer: The affected opponents choose their own cards from their own hands, not randomly. Resolve opponents starting from your left and proceeding clockwise. Test of Humanity must choose something they can actually do: no discard from an empty hand and no loss of a deployed troop they do not have.
answers.evidence: Opponent discards clarification names chooser, source, order and Test of Humanity limits.

answers.answer: After setup is complete and before the first round, Baron Vladimir Harkonnen secretly chooses two of four Baron tokens and places them Faction-side down on the Leader; return the other two to the box unseen. Reveal later as described to gain the reward, only once per game. The summary does not specify the exact moment or procedure for each later reveal.
answers.evidence: Masterstroke clarification gives setup timing, hidden selection and one-time use, but only says reveal ‘later as described.’

answers.answer: Yes. If the Conflict reward gives spice, take it first and use it to play Demand Respect; To the Victor… can also fund it. A win-trigger Intrigue drawn as a victory reward may be played immediately. A first-place tie has no winner, so a win-trigger card cannot be played.
answers.evidence: Demand Respect clarification; Combat tie rule says no win-trigger on first-place tie and reward-drawn win trigger may be immediate.

answers.answer: Yes, zero is allowed when an effect says retreat ‘any number.’ Retreated troops move from Conflict to your garrison; lost troops return to your supply.
answers.evidence: Losing vs. retreating troops clarification.

answers.answer: No. Assassination Mission does not self-trash for its 4 Solari; another effect must trash it. Imperial Spy draws Intrigue only when you use its own self-trash effect, not when another effect trashes it.
answers.evidence: Assassination Mission / Imperial Spy FAQ clarification.

answers.answer: Yes, keep the VP gained when acquiring The Spice Must Flow even if you later trash it. Guild Bankers’ discount applies to each copy acquired that turn.
answers.evidence: The Spice Must Flow / Guild Bankers clarification.

answers.answer: The first condition gives 1 VP for having at least two The Spice Must Flow cards; the second gives a separate 1 VP for having more than each opponent. Both score 2 VP; either alone scores 1 VP; neither scores none. Count cards in your deck and discard pile. Compare each opponent separately; if any one has at least as many as you, the second condition fails, but the first may still score.
answers.evidence: Corner the Market clarification states independent conditions, scoring, deck/discard count and per-opponent comparison.

answers.answer: Ruthless Negotiator triggers only when paying a board space’s printed Solari cost, not a card ability’s Solari cost. Spice Addict is mandatory and only affects spice harvested by sending an Agent to a Maker space, not spice gained by other means.
answers.evidence: Count Ilban / Countess Ariana clarification.

answers.answer: Original base spice is 1 at Imperial Basin, 2 at Hagga Basin, 3 at The Great Flat; accumulated bonus is not base spice. Liet Kynes counts qualifying cards from Agent turns this round and the current Reveal turn, earning 2 Persuasion each.
answers.evidence: Carryall / Liet Kynes clarification.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the set-aside card. You may acquire it by another effect, but the 1-Persuasion discount does not apply then. If you have not acquired it by the end of your next Reveal turn, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: Helena Richese — Manipulate clarification.

answers.answer: Double Cross requires at least one opponent troop in the Conflict, but no troop in your own supply is required. Gun Thopter’s Agent box does not affect an opponent with no garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Double Cross / Gun Thopter clarification.

answers.answer: Shifting Allegiances may lose and gain Influence with the same Faction for net +1, but you must be able to pay the one-Influence loss; a Faction at zero cannot pay. Each Influence track has six spaces; 3 Influence is immediately above the 2-Influence VP space.
answers.evidence: Shifting Allegiances clarification and Faction Influence section.

answers.answer: Recruitment Mission’s acquire destination choice applies only during that round’s Reveal turn, not acquisitions during Agent turns. In the Reveal turn, choose independently for each acquired card whether it goes on top of your deck or into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Recruitment Mission clarification.

answers.answer: Refocus reshuffles your deck if your discard pile is empty. A card drawn during a Reveal turn must immediately be revealed and used during that turn.
answers.evidence: Refocus / Poison Snooper clarification.

answers.answer: Missionaria Protectiva belongs to the Bene Gesserit Faction; after correcting misprints include only two copies in the Imperium deck.
answers.evidence: Missionaria Protectiva erratum.

answers.answer: Yes. Players can score above 12 VP; the printed Score track end is not a limit.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘You can score above 12 VP.’

answers.answer: House Hagal is affected by effects targeting opponents or players if it has the specified resources. It receives no Influence-track bonuses; Signet Ring has no effect in two-player play because those icons are solo-only.
answers.evidence: House Hagal overview and icon rules.

answers.answer: House Hagal acts after each First Player Agent turn only, not after the second human’s turns or after a Reveal turn. Swordmaster can give the First Player a third Agent and allow a third Hagal turn; otherwise its count follows the First Player’s actual Agent turns and available Hagal Agents, not a fixed two-turn limit.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Agent turns paragraph, including Swordmaster and temporary/recalled Agent exceptions.

answers.answer: Ordinary Persuasion cannot buy Foldspace. It requires an acquire-Foldspace icon, normally from the Foldspace board space.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards section: Foldspace requires an acquire-Foldspace icon and cannot be bought with Persuasion.

answers.answer: You retain the City icon and do not get a second Fremen icon. Dispatch an Envoy adds only missing Faction icons; existing icons, including non-Faction icons, remain and it never creates a duplicate.
answers.evidence: Dispatch an Envoy clarification.

answers.answer: Yes. Troops recruited this turn from any source, including Intrigue cards, may be deployed at a Combat space, plus up to two more from your garrison. Existing garrison troops cannot be re-recruited to evade the limit.
answers.evidence: Deploying rule explicitly includes Intrigue-card recruits and forbids re-recruiting garrison troops.

answers.answer: Draw the one card remaining; when unable to draw another, reshuffle your discard pile to form a new deck, then continue drawing until you have three. Cards still face up in play are not in the discard pile; they go to discard at Clean Up, so they are not part of this reshuffle.
answers.evidence: Deck exhaustion says reshuffle discard when unable to draw; Clean Up puts cards in play into discard afterward.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s standard 10-card starting deck and place it face down to the left of the Leader. Shuffle the Intrigue Deck face down; shuffle the Imperium Deck face down and deal 5 face-up Row cards; put Arrakis Liaison, The Spice Must Flow and Foldspace in separate Reserve stacks. Put the Mentat on its side in its space and Alliance tokens on their track marks. Choose the First Player randomly and give them the marker.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, 5 and 9 specify these deck preparations, Row, Reserve stacks, Mentat, Alliance tokens and First Player.

answers.answer: Unused player components in supply should be in clear view of all players. Intrigue cards remain face down, so the summary does not say their faces become public.
answers.evidence: Setup: remaining components in supply ‘in clear view’; Intrigue cards: keep them face down and reveal only when played.

answers.answer: You may spend Persuasion before, between or after Reveal effects; you need not finish all effects first.
answers.evidence: Reveal effects step: may spend Persuasion to acquire cards ‘before, between, or after your Reveal effects.’

answers.answer: City icons access Arrakeen, Carthag, Sietch Tabr and Research Station. Landsraad icons access High Council, Swordmaster, Hall of Oratory, Rally Troops and Mentat. Spice Trade icons access Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, The Great Flat, Secure Contract and Sell Melange.
answers.evidence: Agent icons and board spaces sections enumerate City, Spice Trade and Landsraad spaces.

answers.answer: The First Player marker holder takes the first turn; play proceeds clockwise, one turn at a time. On each turn choose an Agent turn or Reveal turn. Players may Reveal with Agents remaining; after Revealing, they are skipped for the rest of the phase. Phase ends when everyone has Revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns section gives start order, alternation, optional early Reveal and phase end.

answers.answer: The player at 8 wins and gets the top reward; 6 gets second reward; 4 gets no reward because ordinary third place pays only in a 4-player game. In a 4-player game an ordinary third-place finisher gets the third reward.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat specifies rank rewards and third reward only in 4-player games.

answers.answer: If Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, it reveals its combat card first at the start of Combat (reshuffling and revealing again if Reshuffle), then humans may play Combat Intrigue cards. If Hagal has no troop in the Conflict, it has no strength procedure/card reveal.
answers.evidence: House Hagal Combat strength procedure begins ‘if House Hagal has at least one troop’; humans then play Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: The conditions score separately: 1 VP for having at least two The Spice Must Flow cards, and another 1 VP for having more than each opponent. Both score 2 VP; either alone scores 1 VP; neither scores none. Count cards in your deck and discard pile. The second condition compares each opponent separately; if any opponent has at least as many, that condition fails.
answers.evidence: Corner the Market clarification spells out each criterion, points, zones and opponent comparison.

answers.answer: Yes. Sardaukar Legion’s Reveal box can deploy up to 3 troops from your garrison during Reveal effects, before Set Strength, so they count in strength immediately.
answers.evidence: Reveal-turn deployment exception specifically gives Sardaukar Legion as example and timing.

answers.answer: Landsraad Popularity discounts by 1 Solari the printed entry cost of a Landsraad (green) board space when Leto sends an Agent there; apply the discount before paying. Prudent Diplomacy optionally pays 1 spice for 1 Influence with a Faction where an opponent has more Influence than Leto; it cannot target one where no opponent is ahead.
answers.evidence: Duke Leto FAQ clarification states discount scope/timing and Prudent Diplomacy cost/condition.

answers.answer: Choose the Maker space with the most bonus spice; break a tie by total spice (base plus bonus). If no Maker space has bonus spice, reveal another Hagal card instead. Remove all bonus spice from the harvested space and return it to the bank; Hagal keeps none.
answers.evidence: Harvest Spice procedure steps 1 and 3.

answers.answer: Choose two different Factions and gain 1 Influence with each; you cannot put both points into one Faction. This differs from a single generic gain-two-Influence effect, which cannot be split.
answers.evidence: Conditional icons clarification specifically says Machinations ‘Choose two’ means two different Factions, one Influence each.

answers.answer: Master Tactician offers 3 swords OR retreat up to 3 troops; choose one effect, not both. Retreated troops move from the Conflict to your garrison.
answers.evidence: Intrigue card ‘OR’ clarification gives Master Tactician’s alternatives; retreat clarification gives destination.
